newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - July 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Editor of the Sunday Times newspaper, Sinha Ratnatunga, handed a suspended sentence of 18 months and fined 10,000 rupees by the high court for defaming President Chandrika Kumaratunga.
An international military academy for post-graduate studies, to be set up in the Colombo suburb of Sapugaskande in 1998, senior military sources said.
A presidential task force recommends setting up a National Health Commission to implement health policies, and also a Hospital Management Board to run the island's hospitals.
Sunday times editor found guilty of defaming President Kumaratunga and given 18-month jail term suspended for seven years and fined 10,000 rupees.

The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebel torch a refugee ship in northwestern Sri Lanka and abduct nine crew. The ship, which was used to ferry displaced people from Mannar to the northern Jaffna peninsula, had no refugees on board at the time of the attack.
Sunday Times Editor Sinha Ratnatunga, found guilty on Tuesday of defaming President Kumaratunga, to appeal the high court ruling.
If Operation Jaya Sikuru launched in May to open a strategic highway through the Wanni succeeds, LTTE leader Prabhakaran will be isolated in his base in Mulaitivu, defence sources say.
